subject.title: fix(agents): route provider-local-service health probe through fetchWithSsrFGuard

question: Should provider local-service health probes trust only loopback, RFC1918 IPv4, and IPv6 ULA literals under strict guarded fetch, or must configured local DNS/tailnet/non-RFC1918 health URLs remain supported before merge?
rationale: The code fix is bounded, but the PR defines a new security and upgrade boundary for an operator-configured readiness URL that current docs describe broadly.

options.title: Accept literal-private boundary
options.body: Proceed with the current policy after owner review, accepting that non-literal private health URLs may fail closed unless separately supported later.

options.title: Broaden compatibility first
options.body: Ask for explicit support and tests for additional local URL classes such as local DNS, CGNAT/tailnet, or unspecified-bind health URLs before merge.

options.title: Pause for wider SSRF design
options.body: Hold this PR until the exact-host trusted-origin semantics are settled alongside related guarded-fetch work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100835.

recommendation.title: Accept literal-private boundary
recommendation.body: Proceed with the current policy after owner review, accepting that non-literal private health URLs may fail closed unless separately supported later.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` is the strongest current-main owner signal for the provider local-service path from merged PR history.
